record.paper_title: Recent Progress and Open Problems in Algorithmic Convex Geometry
record.original_question: Is there a strongly polynomial algorithm for linear programming, meaning an algorithm whose running time can be bounded polynomially in the dimension and combinatorial input size without dependence on numerical accuracy parameters arising from repeated rescaling?

evidence.quote: In principle, such a dependence can be avoided for linear programming and it is a major open problem to find a strongly polynomial algorithm for solving linear programs.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A linear program is the optimization problem of maximizing a linear functional $c^\top x$ over $\{x \in \mathbb{R}^n : Ax \le b\}$, where $A \in \mathbb{Q}^{m\times n}$, $b \in \mathbb{Q}^m$, and $c \in \mathbb{Q}^n$. A strongly polynomial algorithm for linear programming is an algorithm that:

(i) in the arithmetic model of computation (where each arithmetic operation $+,-,\times,\div$ and each comparison on rational numbers takes unit time) performs a number of operations bounded by a polynomial in the combinatorial input size $m+n$ only (independent of the bit-lengths of the entries of $A$, $b$, $c$);

(ii) when run on a Turing machine, runs in time polynomial in the total bit-length of the input (i.e., is also polynomial in the usual Turing-machine sense); and

(iii) in particular, the number of arithmetic operations does not depend on numerical accuracy parameters and the size of intermediate numbers stays polynomially bounded.

Question: Does there exist such a strongly polynomial algorithm for linear programming?
artifact.status_search_result: This is widely known as Smale's 9th problem and is a longstanding major open problem in optimization and theoretical computer science. As of recent surveys (through 2025), no strongly polynomial algorithm for general linear programming is known; progress exists only for special classes (e.g., LPs with bounded entries, certain combinatorial LPs, MDPs with fixed discount).

status_evidence.title: Smale's problems - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Problem 9: Is there a strongly-polynomial time algorithm which given a linear programming problem decides if it has a solution? — listed as unresolved.
status_evidence.claim: The existence of a strongly polynomial algorithm for linear programming is Smale's 9th problem and remains open.

status_evidence.title: Linear programming - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: There is no known strongly polynomial-time algorithm for linear programming; this is one of the major open problems in the theory of algorithms.
status_evidence.claim: No strongly polynomial algorithm for LP is currently known.
